en.title: Lexicographically Smallest Index Permutation Maximizing the Position-Weighted Sum
en.description:
Return a permutation p of the original indices 1..n that maximizes Σ(i×data[p[i]]), where i runs from 1 to n. If several permutations give the same maximum sum, return the lexicographically smallest index permutation. You return the sequence of original indices, not the sum or the new position of each original element.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains data. The original statement gives no value bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000 and −10^9≤data[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output n one-based original indices in the order of the optimal permutation, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The answers are 3 5 1 4 2, 2 4 1 3 and 3 2 1 respectively. Equal values appear with the smaller original index first.
hints: Sort the original indices by (data[i],i) in ascending order and output the one-based indices.
